external_ask: Search for published results or registry updates for the CanBiome2 trial (NCT06623461) and other large-scale Phase III randomized controlled trials of microbiome interventions in oncology to determine if any have been completed and reported since the publication of the reviewed Phase II studies.
limits: Published primary outcome data (efficacy endpoints such as OS, PFS, or ORR) from a completed Phase III randomized controlled trial of microbiome interventions (e.g., FMT or defined consortia) in ICI-treated solid tumour patients.
question: Are there any completed large-scale Phase III randomized controlled trials of microbiome interventions in ICI-treated solid tumour patients?
still_missing: Published primary outcome data (efficacy endpoints such as OS, PFS, or ORR) from a completed Phase III randomized controlled trial of microbiome interventions (e.g., FMT or defined consortia) in ICI-treated solid tumour patients.
usable_content: Based on the reviewed materials, there are no completed large-scale Phase III randomized controlled trials (RCTs) of microbiome interventions in ICI-treated solid tumour patients. The available evidence consists exclusively of early-phase, non-randomized studies. Specifically, the MITRIC trial (NCT05286294) was a single-arm phase IIa basket trial involving 12 patients with advanced cancers progressing on ICIs; it reported an objective response rate (ORR) of 0% and limited clinical benefit, concluding that FMT does not support efficacy as a salvage therapy in this non-biomarker-driven population. Similarly, the FMT-LUMINate trial is identified as a multicenter, open-label, phase 2 trial (not Phase III) evaluating healthy donor FMT combined with ICIs in NSCLC and melanoma. While FMT-LUMINate reported higher ORRs (80% in NSCLC anti-PD-1 monotherapy; 75% in melanoma dual ICI), it lacked randomization and control groups. Although the authors of FMT-LUMINate mention that findings will be assessed in the ongoing CanBiome2 randomized trial (NCT06623461), the current materials do not report results from any completed Phase III RCT. Therefore, the claim of completed large-scale Phase III RCTs confirming efficacy is not supported by the existing literature base.
